input: nums is a list of n integers in [0,1000], with 2 <= n <= 1000. firstLen and secondLen are positive integers whose sum is at most n. Integer inputs are plain int values excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists and strings are ordinary str values, without subclasses or overloaded behavior. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The maximum sum of two nonoverlapping contiguous subarrays with respective lengths firstLen and secondLen. Either length may appear first; adjacency is allowed. Return the sum only, not indices.
mutation_aliasing: Input entries, their order and both length values remain unchanged. A fresh prefix-sum container is private; the two helper passes share it read-only and keep separate scalar running maxima. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: Prefix sums and final two-window totals are at most 1000000. The evaluated best_first+prefix[end] addition can double-count a prefix before subtraction and is conservatively bounded by 2000000. Prefix differences are nonnegative; all indices, sums and intermediate arithmetic remain exact safe integers.
complexity: O(n) time for prefix construction and two ordered-window passes, with O(n) prefix storage and O(1) helper state. Each pass updates the best first window ending no later than the current second window begins, guaranteeing nonoverlap.
